title: Git Remote Operations
description: Learn how to work with remote repositories and collaborate with others

steps.title: Understanding Remote Repositories
steps.content:
Remote repositories are hosted versions of your project:

Key concepts:
- Remote: A hosted copy of your repository
- Origin: Default name for primary remote
- Upstream: Original repository (if forked)
- Tracking branch: Local branch linked to remote

Common hosting platforms:
- GitHub
- GitLab
- Bitbucket
- Azure DevOps

steps.title: Remote Management
steps.content:
Basic remote operations:

Viewing remotes:
- git remote: List remotes
- git remote -v: Show URLs
- git remote show origin: Detailed info

Modifying remotes:
- git remote add <name> <url>
- git remote rename <old> <new>
- git remote remove <name>
- git remote set-url <name> <url>

Example:
git remote add origin https://github.com/user/repo.git

practical_task.description: Add a remote named 'origin' pointing to your repository. What command did you use?

steps.title: Fetching and Pulling
steps.content:
Getting remote changes:

Fetch operations:
- git fetch: Download objects and refs
- git fetch origin: From specific remote
- git fetch --all: From all remotes
- git fetch --prune: Clean up deleted refs

Pull operations:
- git pull: Fetch and merge
- git pull --rebase: Rebase instead of merge
- git pull origin main: From specific branch

Differences:
- fetch: Safe, doesn't modify working tree
- pull: Combines fetch and merge/rebase

practical_task.description: Fetch changes from remote and view them without merging. What commands did you use?

steps.title: Pushing Changes
steps.content:
Sharing your changes:

Basic push:
- git push: Upload commits
- git push origin main: Specific branch
- git push -u origin main: Set upstream

Advanced options:
- git push --force: Overwrite history (careful!)
- git push --force-with-lease: Safer force push
- git push --tags: Include tags
- git push --all: All branches

Best practices:
- Pull before pushing
- Never force push shared branches
- Use branch protection
- Keep commits clean

practical_task.description: Push your changes and set up tracking. What command sets up tracking on first push?

exercises.question: What is the default name for the main remote?
exercises.explanation: By convention, the primary remote repository is named 'origin' when you clone or set up a repository.

exercises.question: What command downloads changes without merging?
exercises.explanation: git fetch safely downloads remote changes without modifying your working tree, allowing you to review changes before merging.

exercises.question: What command combines fetch and merge?
exercises.explanation: git pull performs a git fetch followed by a git merge (or rebase) to integrate remote changes into your current branch.

exercises.question: What flag sets up branch tracking?
exercises.explanation: The -u or --set-upstream flag establishes a tracking relationship between local and remote branches.
